content: Pediomelum cuspidatum, also referred to as Psoralea cuspidata, is a perennial herb commonly known as the Tall-bread Scurf-pea. This plant is native to the black soil prairies of Texas. It features an inflorescence borne on stems that range from 18 to 40 centimeters in length, which arise from a subterranean stem and a deep, carrot-shaped root measuring 4 to 15 centimeters in length. The leaves of this species are long-petioled and palmately divided into five linear-elliptic leaflets, each measuring 2 to 4 centimeters in length. The flowers, which are light blue and resemble those of pea plants, are produced in condensed spikes that emerge from the leaf axils. Pediomelum cuspidatum typically emerges in late spring. Unlike its smaller and more prolific relative, Pediomelum hypogaeum, this species produces relatively few seeds. The plant is notable for its edible tuberous roots, although some sources describe the taste of these roots as bitter.
